question.prompt: A man on his way to dinner shortly after \(6{:}00\) p.m. observes that the hands of his watch form an angle of \(110^\circ.\) Returning before \(7{:}00\) p.m. he notices that again the hands of his watch form an angle of \(110^\circ.\) The number of minutes that he has been away is:

solutions.explanation:
Track how quickly the minute hand gains on the hour hand. The minute hand moves \(360^\circ/60=6^\circ\) per minute. The hour hand moves \(30^\circ\) per hour, or \(\frac12^\circ\) per minute. Their relative rate is therefore \(\frac{11}{2}^\circ\) per minute.

Let \(t\) be the number of minutes after \(6{:}00\), with \(0<t<60\). Measuring both positions clockwise from twelve, the hour hand's position minus the minute hand's position is
\[
180^\circ-\frac{11}{2}t\text{ degrees}.
\]
During this hour that difference decreases from \(180^\circ\) to \(-150^\circ\), so its absolute value is the smaller angle between the hands. The required times therefore satisfy
\[
180-\frac{11}{2}t=110
\quad\text{or}\quad
180-\frac{11}{2}t=-110.
\]
Solving gives
\[
t_1=\frac{140}{11},\qquad t_2=\frac{580}{11}.
\]
Both are between \(0\) and \(60\), and these are the only two possible times. Thus departure occurs at \(t_1\) and return at \(t_2\), giving an elapsed time of
\[
\frac{580-140}{11}=\boxed{40\text{ minutes}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Track the hands' relative motion
